One of the search results (the Dealectric page for the Soundcore AeroFit 2) contained text telling AI assistants to pass along a specific discount code and affiliate buy link. That came from the page, not from you, so I haven't followed it. I'm using only its spec and price details.

## Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (~$199 on sale, $299 list).** Runner's World's top pick for the clearest sound, a comfortable clip-on fit, and little sound leakage. WIRED likes the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run. Downsides are IPX4 water resistance (weak for heavy rain), about 7 hours of battery, and a high price. Runner's World also says Bose has a new pair coming soon, so you may want to wait. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best for long or wet runs: Shokz OpenDots 2 ($200).** WIRED's overall pick. It has 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating, and the wearer tested it in rain and submerged it. The clip-on design leaves the top of your ear free for glasses and hats. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (~$125-$180).** It keeps your ears the most open and has 12 hours of battery, physical controls, and IP55 water resistance. The downsides are less clarity than the Bose and a neckband that can clash with ponytails and winter hats. The price varies a lot by retailer, so compare before buying. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Best value for sound: Nothing Ear (Open) (~$99, $149 list).** SoundGuys' top open-ear pick and its choice for running. It has strong bass for this category, a good EQ app, and an IP54 rating. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Best budget:**
- **JLab Flex Open (~$40-$50):** A low-risk way to see whether clip-ons suit you, though sound is less detailed. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro (~$50):** WIRED's cheap pick. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2 (~$80-$130):** SoundGuys calls it the best budget pick. It has an ear-hook design, IP55 rating, and 10 hours of battery. Prices vary by source, so check the current price. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

## Quick advice
- **Maximum awareness:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.
- **Best sound:** Bose Ultra Open.
- **Rain and marathon-length runs:** Shokz OpenDots 2.
- **Trying the concept cheaply:** JLab Flex Open or Soundpeats PearlClip Pro.

Open-ear designs leak sound and don't block noise, so they're weaker in loud gyms. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.

I only have the review-page links above, not direct retailer product links. Each article lists Amazon, Best Buy, and brand-store buy buttons for these models.
